geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the abstract taper with a sectionally legible profiled mass so the upper body reads as a continuous programmatic roof/section rather than a purely sculptural reduction.
Use a simple directional section family to strengthen program fit and create a more coherent roof/daylight response.
Orient the section logic to reinforce a clear public-front / private-back organization and avoid the current arbitrary stepped object.

graph_edits.rationale: Align the primary notch/void response to the verified access edge so the public threshold opens toward the street rather than folding away from it.
Increase the notch prominence so the access edge reads as a deliberate public carve instead of a minor incision.
Lower the notch extent to keep the public carve grounded and readable as an entry/court condition rather than a high decorative bite.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant massing idea across views: a bent, stepped, tapering bar with a carved corner and an upper curving/bending gesture. The silhouette is coherent enough to avoid fragmentation, and the repair/containment appears intact. However, the form over-relies on stacked setbacks and a steep sculptural section, so the non-stair quality is weak; it risks reading as an arbitrary stepped object rather than a capacity-bearing neighborhood building. More importantly, the access/frontage response is underdeveloped: the blue access edge is not answered by a clear public void, entry seam, undercut, or terrace legible as a ground threshold. The void logic exists, but it is mostly internalized and not convincingly public. Programmatically, the mass could support neighborhood living in a generic sense, but the section and roof behavior feel more like an abstract sculptural bar than a mixed-use ground-sensitive building with an active street edge. The references support a correction toward a more explicit courtyard/threshold and a cleaner public ground response rather than more slicing.

warnings: The candidate is only moderately legible as neighborhood living because the ground-level public relation is weak.
The blue frontage edge is not strongly activated; current response is closer to a sealed/sculptural mass than a public threshold.
Stepped/tapered section reads as an object strategy more than a programmatic section strategy.
Do not confuse the coherent silhouette with good program fit; section and access logic still fail the hard-pass standard.
